title: Large language models as synthetic clinical experts to inform longitudinal rare-disease modeling
abstract: arXiv:2608.16507v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Due to the limited amount of information, modeling longitudinal rare-disease data can benefit from integrating clinical knowledge. Yet, elicitation of expert knowledge and formalization for model fitting is challenging, in particular due to limited time of clinical experts. To nevertheless make domain knowledge accessible during model fitting, we use large language models (LLMs) as synthetic clinical experts to supervise a variational-autoencoder-based approach that learns low-dimensional latent summaries of visit-level observations. Specifically, LLMs are queried offline on textual descriptions of patient observations to obtain judgments, e.g., the suspected clinical category. To improve the variational autoencoder fit, we train a differentiable surrogate model on these judgments and augment the loss function to encourage reconstructions that preserve the clinical-label distribution of their corresponding input profile. translated_title: 大型语言模型作为合成临床专家以指导纵向罕见疾病建模
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.16507v1 公告类型：新  摘要：由于信息量有限，纵向罕见疾病数据的建模可以从整合临床知识中获益。然而，专家知识的获取和形式化以用于模型拟合具有挑战性，特别是由于临床专家时间有限。为了在模型拟合过程中仍能利用领域知识，我们使用大型语言模型（LLMs）作为合成临床专家，监督一种基于变分自编码器的方法，该方法学习就诊级观察的低维潜在摘要。具体来说，LLMs在离线状态下对患者观察的文本描述进行查询，以获得判断，例如疑似临床类别。为了改进变分自编码器的拟合，我们训练一个可微分的替代模型来处理这些判断，并增强损失函数，以鼓励保留其对应输入配置文件的临床标签分布的重建。在应用中...
tldr: 本文提出利用大型语言模型作为合成临床专家，通过离线查询和替代模型增强变分自编码器，以在数据有限的情况下有效建模纵向罕见疾病并保留临床标签分布。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes using large language models as synthetic clinical experts, enhancing a variational autoencoder via offline queries and a surrogate model to effectively model longitudinal rare diseases with limited data while preserving clinical-label distributions.
